## Revolving Frame Assembly

The revolving frame (5) serves as the primary structural foundation supporting a comprehensive array of operational components. This frame is engineered to accommodate the counterweight (6), which provides essential balance during operation, along with the engine (7) that serves as the primary power source. Additionally, the revolving frame supports a cooling fan (9) and heat exchanger (10), which work in conjunction to manage thermal conditions generated during engine operation. An exterior cover (14) is also mounted on the revolving frame, and this cover is specifically designed to form a machine room (15), creating an enclosed space that houses and protects the internal components from external environmental factors.

## Exhaust Gas Purification System

The exhaust gas purifying device (16) is a critical emissions control component that incorporates a urea selective reduction catalyst (24) as its core functional element. This catalyst system operates in conjunction with a urea water injection valve (26), which is strategically positioned to inject urea water as a reducing agent at a location upstream of the catalyst itself. This upstream injection point is essential for ensuring proper mixing and reaction of the urea water with the exhaust gases before they encounter the selective reduction catalyst, thereby optimizing the efficiency of the emissions reduction process.

## Urea Water Supply System

To facilitate the continuous operation of the exhaust purification process, a urea water supply line (28) is installed to deliver urea water directly to the injection valve (26). This supply line ensures a consistent and reliable flow of the reducing agent necessary for the selective catalytic reduction process to function effectively, maintaining the emissions control system's operational integrity.

## Protective Support Structure

This support member serves a dual purpose: providing structural support for the exterior cover and creating a foundation for additional protective elements. ## Thermal Protection for the Urea Water Supply Line

This specially designed space houses the urea water supply line (28), providing critical protection against the substantial heat generated by the engine (7) during operation. # Construction Machine with Protected Urea Water Supply Line System

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to a construction machine, such as a hydraulic excavator, equipped with an exhaust gas purification system that utilizes urea selective catalytic reduction (SCR) technology to reduce nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions from the engine exhaust.

## Background

Modern construction machines are increasingly equipped with sophisticated exhaust gas purification systems to comply with stringent emission regulations. Among these systems, urea SCR technology has become a widely adopted solution, wherein a urea water solution (commonly known as diesel exhaust fluid) serves as a reducing agent that is injected into the exhaust stream upstream of a urea selective reduction catalyst. Within this catalyst, the urea water decomposes to produce ammonia, which reacts with NOx in the exhaust gas to convert it into harmless nitrogen and water vapor.

To deliver the urea water solution from a storage tank to the injection point near the catalyst, a urea water supply line is routed through the machine, typically in proximity to the engine compartment. However, this arrangement presents a significant technical challenge: the urea water supply line is highly susceptible to thermal degradation when exposed to the substantial heat generated by the engine and surrounding exhaust components. Excessive heat exposure can cause the urea water solution within the line to degrade, crystallize, or otherwise malfunction, potentially compromising the reliability and effectiveness of the entire exhaust purification system. Furthermore, prolonged thermal stress can damage the physical integrity of the supply line itself, leading to leaks or failures that necessitate costly repairs and machine downtime.

Given the compact and space-constrained nature of construction machinery, particularly in the engine compartment and rear machine body areas near the counterweight, there exists a need for an effective solution that protects the urea water supply line from thermal degradation without requiring extensive redesign of the machine's layout or significantly increasing its overall footprint.

## Summary of the Invention

To address the aforementioned problem, the present construction machine incorporates a novel heat shield arrangement specifically designed to protect the urea water supply line from engine-generated heat while maintaining an efficient and compact machine layout.

The construction machine comprises a machine body having a counterweight positioned at a rear portion thereof, and an engine mounted forward of the counterweight. An exhaust gas purification system, including a urea selective reduction catalyst, is provided to treat the engine exhaust, and a urea water supply line extends from a urea water tank to deliver the urea water reducing agent to an injection point associated with the urea selective reduction catalyst.

According to the present disclosure, a horizontal support member is positioned in front of the counterweight, extending in a substantially horizontal direction across the machine body. This support member may serve additional structural functions within the machine, such as supporting other components or reinforcing the machine frame, while simultaneously providing a mounting platform for the heat shield arrangement.

A heat shield cover is mounted on the horizontal support member such that it is positioned in relation to the support member to create a dedicated space between the two components. This space—referred to herein as the "line accommodating space"—is specifically configured to house and route the urea water supply line as it passes through this region of the machine body.

By positioning the urea water supply line within this dedicated space bounded by the horizontal support member and the heat shield cover, the supply line is effectively isolated from direct exposure to heat radiating from the engine and adjacent exhaust system components. The heat shield cover acts as a thermal barrier, deflecting and absorbing radiant heat that would otherwise impinge upon the urea water supply line, while the horizontal support member provides structural support and helps define the boundaries of the protected space.

This configuration offers several advantages. First, it ensures that the urea water solution flowing through the supply line remains within an acceptable temperature range, preventing degradation, crystallization, or other heat-related malfunctions that could compromise the reducing agent's effectiveness. Second, by protecting the physical integrity of the supply line itself, the design reduces the risk of line failure due to thermal stress, thereby enhancing the overall durability and reliability of the exhaust gas purification system. Third, because the heat shield cover is integrated with an existing horizontal support member rather than requiring an entirely separate structural component, this solution can be implemented with minimal impact on the machine's overall size, weight, and manufacturing complexity.

Additionally, the strategic placement of the heat shield cover and support member assembly in front of the counterweight takes advantage of the existing spatial configuration of the construction machine, utilizing an area that might otherwise remain underutilized. This placement also facilitates convenient routing of the urea water supply line from the tank to the injection point while maintaining protection throughout the most heat-critical portion of its path.

## Advantageous Effects

The construction machine described herein thus provides an effective, space-efficient solution to the persistent problem of thermal degradation affecting urea water supply lines in exhaust gas purification systems. By creating a dedicated, shielded pathway between a horizontal support member and a heat shield cover positioned forward of the counterweight, the urea water supply line is reliably protected from engine heat, ensuring consistent delivery of the urea water reducing agent to the selective reduction catalyst. This, in turn, guarantees the sustained reliable operation of the exhaust gas purification system, supporting compliance with emission standards while minimizing maintenance requirements and extending the operational lifespan of the urea supply components.

# On a Revolving

There is something quietly profound about the concept of revolving—the endless turning that brings us back, again and again, to where we began, yet never quite to the same place twice.

Consider the revolving door, that peculiar architectural invention that has become a fixture of city life. It never fully opens nor fully closes; it exists in perpetual motion, admitting and releasing people in the same continuous gesture. To pass through one requires a kind of trust—you must step into its rotation, match its rhythm, and let it carry you forward. It is neither an entrance nor an exit in the traditional sense, but something more fluid: a passage that never stops moving even when no one is using it.

This same principle governs so much of what we call life. The seasons revolve, bringing winter's cold back around after the fading warmth of autumn, yet each winter arrives changed—we are older, the world has shifted, nothing is truly repeated. The Earth itself revolves around the sun, a cosmic clockwork so vast and steady that we forget we are always in motion, spinning through space even as we sit still.

There is also the revolving restaurant, that novelty of mid-century architecture, where diners are lifted high above a city and slowly rotated to take in the full panorama below. The meal becomes secondary to the experience of watching the world turn beneath you—streets sliding past, buildings rising and falling away, the horizon shifting incrementally until, hours later, you find yourself facing the same view you started with, though changed by everything you've seen in between.

Financially, too, we speak of revolving credit—a loan that renews itself, that offers a kind of continuous access rather than a single transaction. It reflects our modern relationship with resources: not fixed, not finite in the moment, but cyclical, replenishing, always available yet never fully spent.

Perhaps what draws us to the idea of revolving is its honest acknowledgment of both change and constancy. To revolve is to move, but not to escape; it is motion without departure. We revolve through habits, relationships, and thoughts—returning to old patterns with new understanding, retracing familiar paths that somehow lead us somewhere new.

In this way, a revolving thing becomes a metaphor for existence itself: never static, yet never truly free of its own orbit. We spin forward not by leaving the past behind, but by carrying it with us, turning it over again and again until it becomes something we can finally see clearly—if only for the moment before it turns away once more.

## Engine Room Layout with Urea SCR Exhaust Gas Purifying Device

**[0001]** Referring now to Fig. 1 and Fig. 2, an engine room 10 of a construction machine according to the present embodiment will be described in detail. The engine room 10 is provided within a rear portion of an upper swing body 1 of the construction machine, and is defined by a partition wall 11 that separates the engine room 10 from an operator's cab (not shown) disposed forwardly thereof. Within the engine room 10, an engine 20 is mounted on a base frame 12, and is disposed such that a crankshaft (not shown) thereof extends substantially in a left-right direction of the construction machine.

**[0002]** An exhaust gas purifying device 30 employing a urea selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system is disposed adjacent to the engine 20 within the engine room 10. The exhaust gas purifying device 30 includes a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC) 31, a diesel particulate filter (DPF) 32 disposed downstream of the DOC 31, a urea mixing pipe 33 disposed downstream of the DPF 32, a urea injection nozzle 34 provided on the urea mixing pipe 33, and an SCR catalyst 35 disposed downstream of the urea mixing pipe 33. An exhaust pipe 21 connected to an exhaust manifold 22 of the engine 20 is coupled to an inlet side of the DOC 31, so that exhaust gas discharged from the engine 20 is introduced into the exhaust gas purifying device 30 via the exhaust pipe 21.

**[0003]** A urea water tank 40 for storing a urea aqueous solution is disposed at a position spaced apart from the exhaust gas purifying device 30 within the engine room 10, or alternatively at an exterior region of the upper swing body 1 adjacent thereto. The urea water tank 40 is connected to the urea injection nozzle 34 via a urea supply pipe 41, and a urea pump unit 42 is interposed partway along the urea supply pipe 41 so as to pressure-feed the urea aqueous solution from the urea water tank 40 to the urea injection nozzle 34. A urea water level sensor 43 and a urea temperature sensor 44 are provided within the urea water tank 40, and detection signals therefrom are transmitted to a controller 50 that controls an injection amount of the urea aqueous solution from the urea injection nozzle 34 in accordance with an operating condition of the engine 20.

**[0004]** A cooling fan 60 is disposed at one end portion of the engine 20 in the left-right direction, and a radiator 61 and a urea water cooling device 62 are disposed so as to face the cooling fan 60, whereby cooling air generated by rotation of the cooling fan 60 is caused to flow through the radiator 61 and the urea water cooling device 62 so as to cool cooling water of the engine 20 and to prevent freezing or deterioration of the urea aqueous solution within the urea water tank 40, respectively. Furthermore, an exhaust port 36 of the exhaust gas purifying device 30 is disposed so as to open toward an upper surface of the engine room 10, and an exhaust gas discharged from the exhaust port 36, after having been purified through the DOC 31, the DPF 32, and the SCR catalyst 35, is released to an exterior of the upper swing body 1 via an exhaust duct 70 provided in an engine hood 13.

**[0005]** With the above-described layout, since the exhaust gas purifying device 30 employing the urea SCR system is disposed in close proximity to the engine 20 while the urea water tank 40 is disposed at a position thermally isolated from the engine 20, it becomes possible to shorten a pipe length of the exhaust pipe 21 so as to suppress a temperature drop of the exhaust gas, while simultaneously suppressing thermal degradation of the urea aqueous solution stored within the urea water tank 40, thereby achieving both an efficient purification performance of the exhaust gas purifying device 30 and an enhanced durability of the urea water tank 40.

# TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION

## HEAT SHIELD STRUCTURE FOR UREA WATER SUPPLY LINE IN WORKING MACHINE

### TECHNICAL FIELD

The present disclosure relates to a heat shield structure for protecting a urea water supply line arranged in proximity to an engine compartment of a working machine, such as an excavator, wherein the urea water supply line is protected from thermal degradation caused by heat radiated and convected from the engine and associated exhaust after-treatment components.

---

### BACKGROUND

Working machines such as hydraulic excavators are commonly equipped with a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) system as part of an exhaust gas after-treatment device, in order to reduce nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions. The SCR system requires a supply of urea water (diesel exhaust fluid, DEF) from a urea water tank to an SCR catalyst unit, typically routed through a urea water supply line comprising a resin tube and associated fittings.

Because the engine compartment houses high-temperature components—including the engine itself, an exhaust manifold, a turbocharger, and an exhaust pipe—the urea water supply line, which is often constrained to a compact routing path near these components due to limited installation space on the machine body, is susceptible to thermal degradation. Excessive heat can cause the urea water within the line to solidify (crystallize) or can damage the resin material of the tube itself, potentially leading to blockage or leakage.

Conventional heat shield covers used to address this issue are typically bulky metal or resin ducts that enclose the entire line. Such structures increase manufacturing cost, complicate assembly, and are difficult to arrange within the confined space adjacent to the engine, cooling fan, and hydraulic pump housing typically found in the engine compartment of an excavator. There is a need for a heat shield structure that provides effective thermal protection while remaining compact, lightweight, and simple to assemble in a narrow engine compartment space.

---

### SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

An object of the present disclosure is to provide a heat shield structure for a urea water supply line that reliably suppresses temperature rise of the urea water within the line, notwithstanding its proximity to high-temperature engine components, while minimizing structural complexity and space requirements.

According to one aspect, a working machine (e.g., an excavator) comprises:

- a machine body having an engine compartment housing an engine and an exhaust after-treatment device including an SCR catalyst;
- a urea water tank storing urea water;
- a urea water supply line connecting the urea water tank to the SCR catalyst, the supply line passing through or adjacent to the engine compartment; and
- a heat shield plate disposed between a heat source (such as the engine, exhaust manifold, turbocharger, or exhaust pipe) and the urea water supply line, the heat shield plate being interposed so as to block direct radiant heat transfer from the heat source toward the supply line, while defining a ventilation gap that allows convective airflow to carry heat away from the vicinity of the supply line.

In a preferred embodiment, the heat shield plate is a single, generally flat or gently curved metal plate mounted to an existing structural member of the engine compartment (such as a bracket, engine cover stay, or frame member), positioned so as to extend along a substantial portion of the length of the urea water supply line that runs closest to the heat source. The heat shield plate is arranged such that the urea water supply line is positioned in a "shadow" region relative to the heat source, i.e., a straight line drawn from any point on the heat source's high-temperature surface to the supply line is interrupted by the heat shield plate.

---

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION

#### 1. Overall Machine Configuration

The working machine according to the present embodiment is a hydraulic excavator comprising a lower travelling body, an upper slewing body mounted rotatably on the lower travelling body, and a working attachment (boom, arm, bucket) attached to the upper slewing body. The upper slewing body includes a machine body frame on which an engine compartment is mounted, the engine compartment being covered by an engine hood.

Within the engine compartment, an engine is mounted, having an exhaust manifold on one side thereof. An exhaust pipe extends from the exhaust manifold to an exhaust after-treatment device, which includes a Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) and an SCR catalyst unit arranged in series along the exhaust gas flow path. A urea water injection nozzle is provided in the exhaust pipe upstream of the SCR catalyst unit, and is connected via a urea water supply line to a urea water tank mounted separately on the machine body, typically alongside a fuel tank.

The urea water supply line comprises a resin tube (e.g., formed of a fluororesin or polyamide-based material) covered in some sections by an insulating sheath, and is routed from the urea water tank, through a gap between the engine compartment side wall and the engine, to the urea water injection nozzle.

#### 2. Heat Shield Plate Configuration

A heat shield plate is disposed within the engine compartment, positioned between the urea water supply line and one or more heat-generating components, including at least one of: the exhaust manifold, the turbocharger, and the exhaust pipe section connecting to the DPF/SCR unit.

The heat shield plate preferably comprises a metal sheet, such as stainless steel or aluminum-coated steel, having a thickness in the range of approximately 0.5 mm to 2.0 mm, chosen to provide sufficient rigidity while remaining lightweight. The surface of the heat shield plate facing the heat source may optionally be provided with a reflective coating or polished finish to enhance reflection of radiant heat, further reducing the thermal load transmitted to the shielded region.

The heat shield plate is fixed by bolts or brackets to an existing rigid structural component within the engine compartment, such as a support bracket for the exhaust pipe, a mounting bracket for the engine, or a partition wall of the engine compartment, such that no dedicated additional frame member is required for supporting the heat shield plate. This configuration reduces the number of components and simplifies the assembly process.

The heat shield plate is dimensioned and positioned so as to extend along substantially the entire length of the portion of the urea water supply line that passes within a predetermined distance (e.g., 100 mm to 300 mm) of the heat source. The plate is oriented substantially parallel to the longitudinal direction of the adjacent portion of the urea water supply line, and is spaced apart from the supply line by a gap sufficient to allow air circulation, thereby preventing heat conducted into the plate from being directly transferred to the tube via contact.

In one embodiment, the heat shield plate includes one or more bent flange portions at its upper and/or lower edges, which project toward the heat source side, forming a partial duct-like configuration that guides cooling airflow (generated by an engine cooling fan or natural convection within the engine compartment) across the surface of the heat shield plate facing the urea water supply line side, further enhancing heat dissipation away from the supply line.

#### 3. Positional Relationship and Effect

The heat shield plate is arranged such that, in a cross-sectional view taken perpendicular to the longitudinal direction of the urea water supply line, the heat shield plate is interposed directly between the heat source and the supply line, blocking a direct line of sight between the two. This arrangement ensures that radiant heat—typically the dominant mode of heat transfer in the confined engine compartment environment—from the exhaust manifold, turbocharger, and/or exhaust pipe cannot directly impinge upon the urea water supply line or its resin tube.

Simultaneously, because the heat shield plate is spaced from both the heat source and the supply line (rather than being sealed on all sides as in a full duct/cover structure), ambient air within the engine compartment, driven by the engine cooling fan, is permitted to flow through the gaps above, below, and to the sides of the heat shield plate. This airflow carries away heat absorbed by the plate itself, preventing significant secondary radiant or convective heating of the urea water supply line from the shield plate itself.

As a result, the urea water supply line is maintained at a temperature below the threshold at which urea water crystallization or resin tube degradation would occur (approximately below 60-80°C in typical operating environments, depending on the SCR system specification), even when the engine compartment ambient temperature during sustained operation approaches or exceeds 100°C in the vicinity of the exhaust components.

#### 4. Additional Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, multiple heat shield plates may be arranged in a stacked or layered configuration with an air gap therebetween, to further reduce heat transfer via a "double-wall" radiant shielding effect, particularly in regions where the urea water supply line passes in very close proximity (e.g., less than 50 mm) to a particularly high-temperature component such as the turbocharger housing.

In another embodiment, the heat shield plate may be integrally formed with, or directly attached to, a bracket that also supports the urea water supply line itself, such that the tube-supporting bracket and the heat shield function are combined into a single component, further reducing part count and assembly time.

In yet another embodiment, a temperature sensor may be provided on or near the urea water supply line downstream of the heat shield plate, operatively connected to a machine controller, such that if a detected temperature exceeds a predetermined threshold, the controller may activate a cooling fan at increased speed or issue a warning to the operator via a display device.

---

### ADVANTAGES

The heat shield structure according to the present disclosure provides the following advantages over conventional full-enclosure duct-type heat shield covers:

1. **Reduced weight and cost**: A single flat or simply-shaped plate requires less material and manufacturing complexity than a fully enclosed duct.
2. **Simplified assembly**: By mounting the heat shield plate to existing structural brackets, no additional support frame is required, reducing the number of parts and assembly steps.
3. **Effective heat blocking with airflow utilization**: By blocking direct radiant heat transfer while permitting convective air circulation, the heat shield plate achieves effective thermal protection without trapping heat around the urea water supply line, which can occur in fully enclosed shield structures.
4. **Compact configuration**: The heat shield plate can be shaped and positioned to fit within the limited space available in the engine compartment of a compact working machine such as a small or medium-sized hydraulic excavator, without interfering with maintenance access to the engine or exhaust after-treatment device.

---

### CLAIMS (Illustrative, Non-Exhaustive)

**Claim 1.** A working machine comprising:
an engine compartment housing an engine and an exhaust after-treatment device including a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) catalyst;
a urea water tank;
a urea water supply line connecting the urea water tank to an injection nozzle upstream of the SCR catalyst, at least a portion of the urea water supply line being disposed within the engine compartment in proximity to a heat source; and
a heat shield plate disposed between the heat source and the urea water supply line, the heat shield plate blocking direct radiant heat transfer from the heat source to the urea water supply line while defining a gap permitting airflow between the heat shield plate and at least one of the heat source and the urea water supply line.

**Claim 2.** The working machine according to claim 1, wherein the heat shield plate is mounted to an existing structural bracket within the engine compartment without requiring a dedicated support frame.

**Claim 3.** The working machine according to claim 1, wherein the heat shield plate comprises a bent flange portion configured to guide cooling airflow across a surface of the heat shield plate facing the urea water supply line.

**Claim 4.** The working machine according to claim 1, wherein the heat source comprises at least one of an exhaust manifold, a turbocharger, and an exhaust pipe of the engine.

# Heat Shield Assembly for Urea Water Line Protection

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to construction machinery, and more particularly to a heat shielding arrangement for protecting fluid conduits, such as a urea water supply line, from thermal radiation and convective heat generated by an engine mounted on a revolving frame of a working machine.

## Background

In construction machines such as hydraulic excavators, an engine is typically mounted on a revolving frame together with various auxiliary components, including a urea water tank and associated supply lines forming part of a selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system for exhaust after-treatment. The urea water line, which conveys a urea-based reducing agent to the exhaust treatment device, is susceptible to thermal degradation and freezing/thawing performance issues when exposed to excessive heat radiating from the engine or associated exhaust components. It is therefore desirable to provide a structural arrangement that shields the urea water line from such heat while maintaining structural rigidity and accommodating routing constraints within the confined space of the revolving frame.

## Summary of the Invention

According to an aspect of the present invention, there is provided a construction machine comprising a revolving frame, an engine mounted on the revolving frame, a urea water line disposed proximate the engine for supplying urea water to an exhaust treatment system, a horizontal support member mounted on the revolving frame and extending in a lateral direction beneath the urea water line, and a heat shield cover mounted on the horizontal support member so as to be interposed between the engine and the urea water line, thereby blocking heat radiated from the engine from reaching the urea water line.

## Detailed Description

### Overall Configuration

Referring to the drawings, a construction machine according to an embodiment includes a lower traveling body and an upper revolving structure rotatably mounted on the lower traveling body. The upper revolving structure includes a revolving frame constituting a base structure on which various components, including an engine, a hydraulic pump, a urea water tank, and an exhaust treatment device, are mounted.

The engine is mounted on the revolving frame and includes an exhaust manifold and associated exhaust piping that generate substantial heat during operation. A urea water line, formed of a flexible hose or tube, extends from the urea water tank to an injection unit provided in the exhaust treatment device, passing in the vicinity of the engine.

### Horizontal Support Member

A horizontal support member is fixedly mounted on the revolving frame at a position adjacent to the engine. The horizontal support member extends substantially in a horizontal direction, preferably in a lateral or width direction of the revolving frame, so as to bridge a gap between structural members of the revolving frame. The horizontal support member may be configured as a beam, bracket, or plate-like structural member having sufficient rigidity to support additional components mounted thereon, and preferably comprises a metal material such as steel.

In the illustrated embodiment, the horizontal support member is disposed at a height position below the urea water line and above or laterally adjacent to a heat-generating portion of the engine, such that the horizontal support member is interposed, at least in part, in a heat propagation path extending from the engine toward the urea water line.

### Heat Shield Cover

A heat shield cover is mounted on an upper surface, or other suitable surface, of the horizontal support member. The heat shield cover comprises a plate-like member preferably formed of a heat-resistant and/or heat-reflective material, such as a stainless steel sheet, an aluminum sheet, or a composite material having a heat-insulating layer.

The heat shield cover is disposed so as to extend along the horizontal support member in the lateral direction, thereby covering a region between the engine and the urea water line over a sufficient span to intercept radiant heat emitted from the engine. The heat shield cover is oriented such that a heat-facing surface thereof faces the engine, while an opposite surface thereof faces, or is disposed proximate to, the urea water line, such that the urea water line is positioned on a side of the heat shield cover opposite the engine.

The heat shield cover is preferably fixed to the horizontal support member by fastening members, such as bolts, or by welding, so as to be removably or fixedly attached thereto. In an embodiment, the heat shield cover includes a bent or flanged edge portion configured to be secured to the horizontal support member, thereby enhancing rigidity of the heat shield cover and facilitating ease of attachment and detachment during maintenance operations.

### Positional Relationship and Technical Effect

With the above-described arrangement, the horizontal support member functions not only as a structural member supporting peripheral components on the revolving frame, but also as a mounting base for the heat shield cover, whereby the heat shield cover is reliably positioned in the heat propagation path between the engine and the urea water line without requiring a dedicated independent support structure.

The heat shield cover, being mounted on the horizontal support member, blocks and/or reflects heat radiated from the engine, an exhaust manifold, or associated high-temperature components, thereby preventing said heat from directly impinging on the urea water line. This arrangement suppresses excessive temperature rise of the urea water line, thereby preventing thermal degradation of the urea water and/or the material forming the urea water line, and ensuring stable operation of the exhaust treatment system.

Furthermore, because the heat shield cover is supported by the horizontal support member already provided on the revolving frame for structural or other purposes, the overall number of components and the complexity of the machine can be minimized, while efficiently utilizing the limited space available on the revolving frame.

### Alternative Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, the heat shield cover may be formed integrally with the horizontal support member, for example, by forming the horizontal support member itself with a heat-resistant coating or heat-insulating layer on a surface thereof facing the engine, such that the horizontal support member itself functions as the heat shield cover.

In another embodiment, a plurality of heat shield covers may be mounted on the horizontal support member at spaced intervals along the lateral direction, so as to correspond to a routing path of the urea water line, which may include bent or curved portions.

In yet another embodiment, the heat shield cover may include a ventilation gap or louvered portion configured to promote air circulation between the engine and the heat shield cover, thereby further dissipating heat and enhancing the heat-shielding effect through convective cooling in addition to radiant heat blocking.

It is to be understood that the specific configuration, material, and mounting structure of the heat shield cover and the horizontal support member may be modified without departing from the scope of the present invention, provided that the heat shield cover is disposed so as to be interposed between the engine and the urea water line so as to protect the urea water line from heat generated by the engine.

## Claims (Illustrative)

**Claim 1.** A construction machine comprising:
a revolving frame;
an engine mounted on the revolving frame;
a urea water line configured to supply urea water to an exhaust treatment device, the urea water line being disposed in a vicinity of the engine;
a horizontal support member mounted on the revolving frame; and
a heat shield cover mounted on the horizontal support member and interposed between the engine and the urea water line so as to block heat radiated from the engine from reaching the urea water line.

**Claim 2.** The construction machine according to claim 1, wherein the horizontal support member extends in a lateral direction of the revolving frame and is positioned beneath the urea water line.

**Claim 3.** The construction machine according to claim 1, wherein the heat shield cover comprises a plate-like member formed of a heat-resistant material and is fixed to an upper surface of the horizontal support member.

**Claim 4.** The construction machine according to claim 1, wherein the heat shield cover is detachably fixed to the horizontal support member by fastening members.

**Claim 5.** The construction machine according to claim 1, wherein the horizontal support member and the heat shield cover are formed integrally as a single member having a heat-insulating surface facing the engine.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an engineering disclosure passage for a hydraulic excavator's exhaust after-treatment system, covering the urea selective reduction catalyst, injection valve, and supply line routing with heat protection.
counterfactuals.output:
# Exhaust After-Treatment System for Hydraulic Excavator Engine Assembly

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to an exhaust gas after-treatment system for a hydraulic excavator power unit, and more particularly to an arrangement of a selective catalytic reduction (SCR) device, a urea injection valve, and a diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) supply line configured with thermal protection measures to ensure reliable reductant delivery under the harsh thermal and vibrational environment of a construction machine engine compartment.

## Background

Modern hydraulic excavators employing diesel engines compliant with stringent emission regulations require after-treatment systems capable of reducing nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions through selective catalytic reduction. Such systems inject a urea-water solution (DEF) into the exhaust stream upstream of an SCR catalyst, where the urea decomposes into ammonia and reacts with NOx to produce nitrogen and water vapor. However, the confined engine compartment of an excavator, combined with proximity to high-temperature exhaust components, presents challenges in routing the DEF supply line and protecting the injection valve from thermal degradation, urea crystallization, and vibration-induced fatigue failure.

## Summary of the Disclosure

According to one embodiment, the after-treatment system comprises an SCR catalyst unit disposed within an exhaust muffler casing mounted on the upper structure of the excavator, positioned downstream of a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC) and, where applicable, a diesel particulate filter (DPF). The SCR catalyst is housed in a cylindrical catalyst carrier retained within the muffler shell by a mounting bracket that isolates the assembly from direct chassis-transmitted vibration through an intervening cushion or elastic support member.

A urea injection valve is mounted to an injection boss formed on, or welded to, the exhaust pipe or muffler inlet section at a position upstream of the SCR catalyst and sufficiently distant from the turbocharger outlet to allow adequate mixing while avoiding valve-tip overheating. The injection valve is oriented such that its spray axis intersects the exhaust gas flow at an angle promoting atomization and uniform distribution of the urea-water solution across the catalyst inlet face, thereby minimizing the risk of deposit formation on the pipe wall.

The DEF supply line, connecting a DEF tank to the injection valve via a supply pump and dosing module, is routed along the machine's upper frame or counterweight-side structure at a distance from the exhaust pipe, turbocharger, and muffler outer surface sufficient to maintain the DEF below its thermal decomposition threshold. Where the supply line must cross beneath or adjacent to a high-temperature exhaust-related component, a heat-insulating cover—comprising a metal shield plate, a heat-resistant fabric wrap, or a double-walled tube with an air gap—is interposed between the line and the heat source. The insulating cover is fixed independently of the DEF line itself, such as to a bracket secured to the vehicle frame, so that thermal expansion or vibration of the exhaust system does not transmit direct mechanical loading to the supply line or its connectors.

## Detailed Description

### SCR Catalyst Arrangement

The SCR catalyst carrier is preferably formed of a honeycomb ceramic or metallic substrate coated with a vanadium-based or zeolite-based catalytic material, retained within a stainless-steel outer can. The can is joined to the muffler body by a flanged connection permitting disassembly for catalyst replacement during scheduled maintenance. A mat-type mounting material surrounds the catalyst carrier to accommodate thermal expansion differential between the ceramic substrate and the metal casing while providing a seal against exhaust gas bypass.

### Injection Valve Configuration

The urea injection valve is a solenoid-actuated metering device receiving a pressurized DEF supply and pulse-width-modulated electrical control signals from an after-treatment control module. The valve body is fitted with a cooling air jacket or is positioned to receive ambient cooling airflow from the engine compartment fan to prevent urea crystallization at the injector tip during hot soak conditions following engine shutdown. The injection valve connector and wiring harness are routed away from direct exhaust radiant heat and secured to prevent chafing against adjacent structural members.

### Supply Line Routing and Heat Protection

The DEF supply line is preferably a resin or reinforced rubber hose selected for chemical compatibility with urea solution and resistance to thermal aging. The routing path is selected to maximize clearance from the exhaust manifold, turbocharger housing, and muffler outer wall, generally maintaining a minimum standoff distance determined through thermal analysis to keep the line surface temperature below the urea decomposition point during continuous operation.

In sections where routing constraints necessitate closer proximity to heat-generating components, a heat shield is installed between the DEF line and the heat source. The heat shield may take the form of:

1. A rigid metal plate with standoff spacers, reflecting radiant heat away from the supply line;
2. A wrap-around insulating sleeve of glass-fiber or ceramic-fiber material enclosing the line itself; or
3. A double-wall tube configuration in which the DEF line is enclosed within an outer protective conduit, with an air gap serving as a thermal buffer.

The heat shield and its mounting bracket are preferably attached to the machine frame or muffler bracket independently of the DEF line clamps, such that the shield's own thermal expansion and any exhaust-induced vibration are not transmitted into the supply line, thereby reducing fatigue stress at hose fittings and quick-connect couplings. Additionally, the supply line clamps are spaced at intervals selected to prevent resonance-induced flexing during machine operation, and clamp materials incorporating a vibration-damping cushion may be employed at each securing point.

### Operational Advantages

This configuration provides several advantages, including: (1) preventing thermal degradation of the DEF solution during transport to the injection valve, (2) reducing the risk of urea crystallization and consequent injector clogging, (3) improving serviceability of the SCR catalyst unit and injection valve through accessible mounting arrangements, and (4) enhancing the durability of the DEF supply line under the vibration and thermal cycling conditions typical of hydraulic excavator operation, including operation in ambient temperature extremes and extended idling conditions.

## Alternative Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, the injection valve may be integrated into a mixing pipe section separate from the muffler assembly, positioned along the exhaust pipe between the engine and the muffler, with the SCR catalyst remaining housed within the muffler. In yet another embodiment, the DEF supply line may incorporate an electrically heated trace element controlled by the after-treatment control module to actively maintain line temperature above the urea freezing point in cold-climate operation, supplementing the passive heat-shielding measures described above.

It is to be understood that the foregoing description is illustrative and not restrictive, and that various modifications to the arrangement, materials, and configuration of the components described may be made without departing from the scope of the present disclosure.

# Construction Vehicle Machine Room: SCR System and Urea Water Line Heat-Shielding Structure

## Component Description with Reference Labels

### Overall Machine Room Assembly

**(1)** Machine room housing – the main enclosure structure that houses the engine, exhaust after-treatment system, and associated piping

**(2)** Engine – primary power source generating exhaust gases requiring after-treatment

**(3)** Exhaust pipe/manifold – conducts exhaust gases from the engine toward the after-treatment system

**(4)** SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction) system – the after-treatment unit that reduces NOx emissions using urea water (DEF/AdBlue) injection

**(5)** SCR catalyst housing/case – outer casing containing the catalyst substrate

### Urea Water Injection and Supply System

**(6)** Urea water tank – storage reservoir for the urea solution (DEF)

**(7)** Urea water supply pump/pump module – pressurizes and delivers urea solution from tank to injector

**(8)** Urea water line (supply line) – piping/tubing that transports urea water from the tank to the injector nozzle

**(9)** Urea water injector – nozzle device that injects metered urea solution into the exhaust stream upstream of the SCR catalyst

**(10)** Urea water return line – piping that returns excess urea solution back to the tank

**(11)** Urea water line connector/joint – coupling fittings connecting line segments

### Heat-Shielding Structure for Urea Water Line

**(12)** Heat shield cover (upper) – protective plate positioned above the urea water line to block direct radiant heat from the exhaust pipe/engine

**(13)** Heat shield cover (lower/side) – supplementary shielding plate enclosing the lateral or lower side of the urea line

**(14)** Heat shield bracket – structural mounting bracket that supports and positions the heat shield covers relative to the urea line and machine room frame

**(15)** Air gap/insulation space – the clearance maintained between the heat shield and the urea water line to allow air circulation and reduce conductive heat transfer

**(16)** Heat-resistant insulation material – layer of insulating material (e.g., ceramic fiber, glass wool) attached to the inner surface of the heat shield for additional thermal protection

**(17)** Fastening bolts/clips – hardware securing the heat shield covers and brackets to the machine room frame or adjacent structural members

**(18)** Heat shield mounting flange – flange section of the heat shield used for bolting to the bracket or frame

### Surrounding Structural Members

**(19)** Machine room frame/support member – structural framework to which the heat shield brackets and piping clamps are affixed

**(20)** Pipe clamp/holder – fastening device that secures the urea water line in position relative to the heat shield, preventing vibration-induced wear

**(21)** Cooling air duct/vent opening – ventilation opening in the machine room housing that promotes airflow to dissipate heat around the urea line and heat shield assembly

**(22)** Partition wall – internal divider within the machine room separating the high-temperature exhaust/SCR zone from the urea line routing area, providing an additional layer of thermal isolation

---

### Functional Summary

The heat-shielding structure **(12–18)** is positioned between the high-temperature exhaust pipe **(3)**/SCR unit **(4)** and the urea water line **(8)**, forming a thermal barrier. The shield cover **(12, 13)** is mounted via brackets **(14)** to the machine room frame **(19)**, maintaining an air gap **(15)** and incorporating insulation **(16)** to prevent the urea solution from reaching temperatures that would cause thermal decomposition or crystallization within the line **(8)**, ensuring reliable SCR system **(4)** operation and consistent NOx reduction performance.
